newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade light at $65-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade light at $65-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade was extremely light at $65.00 per cwt, unchanged from Wednesday's massive trading volume, which depleted most showlists, feedlot sources said.
Sales Thursday were residual at about 200 head in Kansas and not really enough to test the market, compared with nearly 83,000 traded on Wednesday, they said.
Wednesday's sales were the second largest one-day trading volume for Kansas, behind the record of 88,000 set in September 1995, USDA records showed.
Sales in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area Thursday were about 500 head following 78,700 on Wednesday, the sources said.

The week to date estimate for the Panhandle was 130,500 head, compared with 75,000 a week ago. Kansas week to date movement was pegged at 127,200 head, compared with 64,500 a week ago, USDA statistics showed.

Fed cattle prices were supported by strong demand from packers who were short on live inventories, the feedlot sources said. A large number of cattle sold were earmarked for this week's slaughter and were being shipped early, they said.
Normal pickups are about seven days after cattle are sold, the feedlot sources said.
